Kevin Trudeau puts this question to a Harvard-trained cardiologist: are there people with a cholesterol count of 600, 700, even 800 who never get blocked arteries, never have a stroke or heart attack?

The doctor's answer: yes. People tested with some of the highest cholesterol counts doctors see, 600 to 800, with no heart disease their entire life, living to be 90 years old.

His point: a high number on a chart doesn't automatically mean a blocked artery or a shorter life.
